source_text:
Οὐ διατάσσομαι ὑμῖν ὡς ὤν τις. εἰ γὰρ καὶ δέδεμαι ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι, οὔπω ἀπήρτισμαι ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ: νῦν γὰρ ἀρχὴν ἔχω τοῦ μαθητεύεσθαι, καὶ προσλαλῶ ὑμῖν ὡς συνδιδασκαλίταις μου. ἐμὲ γὰρ ἔδει ὑφ̓ ὑμῶν ὑπαλειφθῆναι πίστει, νουθεσίᾳ, ὑπομονῇ, μακροθυμίᾳ.
ἀλλ’ ἐπεὶ ἡ ἀγάπη οὐκ ἐᾷ με σιωπᾶν περὶ ὑμῶν, διὰ τοῦτο προέλαβον παρακαλεῖν ὑμᾶς, ὅπως συντρέχητε τῇ γνώμῃ τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ γὰρ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὸ ἀδιάκριτον ἡμῶν ζῆν, τοῦ πατρὸς ἡ γνώμη, ὡς καὶ οἱ ἐπίσκοποι, οἱ κατὰ τὰ πέρατα ὁρισθέντες, ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ γνώμῃ εἰσίν.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch writing as a prisoner on his way to martyrdom in Rome, has just praised the Ephesians' unity under their bishop and now explains why he writes to them as a fellow learner rather than as an authority.
pass_a_gloss: I do not give orders to you as if I were someone. For even if I have been bound in the Name, I am not yet perfected in Jesus Christ. For now I have a beginning of being discipled, and I speak with you as with my fellow disciples. For I ought to have been anointed by you with faith, admonition, endurance, patience. But since love does not permit me to be silent about you, for this reason I took the initiative to exhort you, so that you may run together with the purpose of God. For also Jesus Christ, our inseparable life, is the purpose of the Father, just as also the bishops, who have been appointed to the farthest bounds, are in the purpose of Jesus Christ.

choices.why: Keeps the modest, self-effacing force of the Greek idiom, which denies any claim to authority.
rejected: as if I were an authority

choices.why: The capitalized Name preserves the absolute use of ὄνομα for the name of Christ, matching Ignatius's usage elsewhere.
Renders the perfect passive as a present state of incompleteness, keeping the contrast with being bound.
rejected: I have not yet been made complete

choices.english: I have a beginning of being discipled
choices.why: Keeps the noun ἀρχή and the passive infinitive, preserving the idea that discipleship is just starting for him.
rejected: I am only beginning to be a disciple

choices.english: run together with the purpose of God
choices.why: The verb συντρέχω means to run together or converge; keeping the metaphor preserves Ignatius's image of shared movement toward God's will.
rejected: agree with the purpose of God
be in harmony with God's purpose

choices.why: The articular infinitive ζῆν functions as a substantive; the adjective ἀδιάκριτον means inseparable or undivided, describing Christ as the life that cannot be divided from us.
rejected: the life we cannot be separated from

pass_b_english: I am not giving you orders as if I were someone important. Even though I am bound in the Name, I am not yet perfected in Jesus Christ. Right now I am only beginning my training as a disciple, and I speak to you as to my fellow disciples. It was I who needed to be anointed by you with faith, admonition, endurance, and patience.

But since love does not allow me to keep silent about you, I have taken the initiative to urge you to run together with the purpose of God. For Jesus Christ, our inseparable life, is the purpose of the Father, just as the bishops appointed to the farthest bounds of the earth are in the purpose of Jesus Christ.

last_rejected.why: ἀδιάκριτον means 'undivided' or 'indivisible,' not 'inseparable'—a different concept about unity, not attachment.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀδιάκριτον = indivisible/undivided; 'inseparable' is an acceptable rendering, not a meaning change

problems.quote: I am only at the beginning of being discipled
problems.why: 'Being discipled' is awkward; likely means 'being trained as a disciple.'
problems.fix: Use 'beginning my training as a disciple.'

edits.old: Right now I am only at the beginning of being discipled
edits.new: Right now I am only at the beginning of my training as a disciple

problems.quote: For Jesus Christ, our inseparable life, is the purpose of the Father, just as the bishops appointed to the farthest bounds of the earth are in the purpose of Jesus Christ.
problems.why: 'Inseparable life' is awkward; 'purpose' (telos) twice in one sentence with different senses is confusing.
problems.fix: 'Our inseparable life' → 'our life that cannot be separated from us'; clarify second 'purpose.'

edits.old: For Jesus Christ, our inseparable life, is the purpose of the Father, just as the bishops appointed to the farthest bounds of the earth are in the purpose of Jesus Christ.
edits.new: For Jesus Christ, our life that cannot be separated from us, is the purpose of the Father, just as the bishops appointed to the farthest bounds of the earth are in the purpose of Jesus Christ.

fixed: Changed 'our inseparable life' to 'our life that cannot be separated from us' to clarify the meaning of ἀδιάκριτον. The second 'purpose' is a faithful rendering of γνώμῃ and is not confusing in context; no change needed.

problems.quote: For Jesus Christ, our life that cannot be separated from us, is the purpose of the Father, just as the bishops appointed to the farthest bounds of the earth are according to the purpose of Jesus Christ.
problems.why: Two unlike things equated; 'purpose' used oddly; sentence breaks down.
problems.fix: Clarify: bishops extend Christ's purpose geographically.

problems.why: Different English terms for companions or fellow Christians may read as distinct categories.
problems.fix: Use 'fellow servants' or 'companions' consistently for the same Greek concept.

edits.old: For Jesus Christ, our life that cannot be separated from us, is the purpose of the Father, just as the bishops appointed to the farthest bounds of the earth are according to the purpose of Jesus Christ.
edits.new: For Jesus Christ, our life that cannot be separated from us, is the purpose of the Father, just as the bishops appointed to the farthest bounds of the earth are in the purpose of Jesus Christ.

fixed: The sentence does not equate two unlike things; it states that Christ is the Father's purpose and that the bishops are in Christ's purpose. The English 'according to the purpose' is slightly off; the source has 'ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ γνώμῃ εἰσίν' (are in the purpose of Jesus Christ). Changed 'according to the purpose' to 'in the purpose' to match the source more closely.
No 'spiritual family' appears in this section; the source uses 'συνδιδασκαλίταις' (fellow disciples), which is already rendered as 'fellow disciples'. No edit needed.

polish.changed: Clarified the awkward phrase 'being discipled' to 'training as a disciple,' and smoothed the opening clause 'as if I were someone' to 'as if I were someone important' to make the implied contrast natural in English.

notes.quote: I am only at the beginning of being discipled
notes.why: 'Being discipled' is awkward; likely means 'being trained as a disciple.'
notes.fix: Use 'beginning my training as a disciple.'

polish.changed: Clarified the final clause by rendering 'in the purpose of Jesus Christ' as 'according to the purpose of Jesus Christ,' making the relationship between the bishops and Christ's purpose clear and natural in English.

notes.quote: the bishops appointed to the farthest bounds of the earth are in the purpose of Jesus Christ
notes.why: Sentence structure is awkward; 'in the purpose of' is unclear English for 'according to the purpose/plan of'.
notes.fix: Revise to 'are appointed according to the purpose of Jesus Christ'.

polish.changed: Clarified the final sentence by making 'our inseparable life' an appositive for Jesus Christ, so the comparison between Christ as the Father's purpose and the bishops as Christ's purpose reads naturally. Also smoothed 'beginning my training' and removed the awkward 'cannot be separated from us' phrasing.

notes.quote: For Jesus Christ, our life that cannot be separated from us, is the purpose of the Father, just as the bishops appointed to the farthest bounds of the earth are according to the purpose of Jesus Christ.
notes.why: Two unlike things equated; 'purpose' used oddly; sentence breaks down.
notes.fix: Clarify: bishops extend Christ's purpose geographically.

notes.fix: Use 'fellow servants' or 'companions' consistently for the same Greek concept.
